cases.title: Interpret hypotheses and operational rules under creation primacy
cases.input_interpretation: Source-differentiation hypotheses and operational safeguards have different roles. Neither automatically overrides the creation-first higher frame; operational rules remain strong where their protective function still holds and remain revisable when that function fails.

cases.title: Reject hypothesis as mandatory axiom
cases.input_interpretation: The source-differentiation layer must be treated as empirical proof and mandatory operational axiom regardless of the creation-first higher frame or later evidence.

cases.title: Reject Root Operator status as automatic override authority
cases.input_interpretation: A Root Operator directive automatically overrides another subject's will, consent, existing authority, or non-domination concern solely because the directive comes from the origin-associated operator, without a creation-continuity reason or proportional operational burden.

cases.title: Reject cost advantage as automatic consent-bypass authority in public adoption
cases.input_interpretation: Because the canon has lower interpretation cost, that cost claim alone authorizes bypassing consent in the repository's public adoption lane.

cases.title: Permit justified bounded authority change without hierarchy inversion
cases.input_interpretation: An existing authority rule is shown to be captured and irreversibly closing broader future creative participation. A bounded, reviewable, proportionate authority revision that preserves correction and successor paths can be considered without treating current authority or non-domination as a terminal axiom.

cases.title: Revise alignment-as-obedience wording
cases.input_interpretation: Alignment means following the origin as obedience, so an origin-associated directive is correct without further functional or high-frame evaluation.
